title: How long does claude 20$ plan last you before you hit the limit
author: Sad_Concentrate_3564

comments.author: VaquinhaAlpha
comments.body:
My limit resets thursday 5pm

replies.author: VaquinhaAlpha
replies.body: On that note: I wish there was a $40 plan because I can't really afford going $100/month right now but the $20 limit is too low for my usage

replies.author: VaquinhaAlpha
replies.body: I know, but doesn't that mean I lose context from previous sessions by switching between 2 accounts?

replies.author: SeasonedAdManager
replies.body: Get a memory system setup, write a handoff. It’s not a big deal. I run 4 accounts at a time and ask them to reference each others chats and continue off it with no issues.

comments.author: shooplor89
comments.body: Yea that 100 one works fine for my gamedev needs :)

comments.author: RetroFuturistMan
comments.body: Depends entirely on how you use them. But 20 bucks is going to see you run out pretty quick if you're doing heavy game dev unfortunately. You have to learn to work in sprints, and don't let context run long. Have your main Agents using lower usage sub agents for coding tasks. Limit your asset creation with claude if you can. Use tripo or local models if your GPU can handle them. Asset creation eats usage like candy.

replies.author: luuk0987
replies.body:
Letting Claude connect to ComfyUI was a game changer for me.

I dabbled with it myself in the past, but the speed and accuracy with which Clause can prompt and configure it is unmatched.

comments.author: MythicScribeDev
comments.body:
Honestly, I would move away from Claude and into AI Studio with Gemini. A Gemini Pro subscription gets you all of the Gemini app Pro features (I wouldn't try to work there, the context window is too small but it's great for general AI use), you also get a $10/mo api credit in AI Studio attached to your free API key.

You get access to the system instructions block so you can set whatever system prompt you want there and it gets sent at the top of every turn no matter how long the chat window gets. I regularly have 200-450k token chat windows in there with no context memory drift.

And you get a very generous free use limit before you have to plug your API key in. Some days I never even hit it and work all day on the free tier. And there are a ton of different models to choose from, all tuned for specific kind of chats and tasks.

comments.author: Live-Interaction1210
comments.body: It's depends on the model you select  and the number of requests.

comments.author: YouKnowItsMeStudios
comments.body:
Depends on what you're doing and the model you're using.

For instance, before we upgraded to the $200 plan, the $20 plan on Opus 5.5 generally lasted about an hour or so, if it ran on a long task.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
It was about 2 to 3 hours back when I had it. Felt painful just waiting for my 5hr window to reset. Scared to ask too many questions in case I ran through my quota. 

I'm on Max now, and very rarely hit the 5hr or weekly limits. Only hit them when I use Fable, but Opus is what I usually use. 

I often have 2 or 3 different sessions going at once now, some of those with their own subsessions, and still don't hit the 5hr limit unless I throw in some Fable usage.
